entries.title: Keep User Account Control enabled
entries.description: Ensures Admin Approval Mode (UAC) is on for all administrators by pinning EnableLUA to 1.
entries.rationale: With UAC off, administrator processes run fully elevated and Store apps, Edge and other AppContainer sandboxes stop working. The app never sets this to 0; it only asserts the secure value.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode

entries.title: Apply UAC to the built-in Administrator account
entries.description: Puts the built-in Administrator account into Admin Approval Mode by setting FilterAdministratorToken to 1, so it also gets elevation prompts.
entries.rationale: Without this, the built-in Administrator (if enabled) runs everything fully elevated with no prompt. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS all enable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account

sideEffects: If the built-in Administrator account is enabled, it now receives UAC prompts instead of running silently elevated.

entries.title: Prompt admins for consent on the secure desktop
entries.description: Sets the elevation prompt for administrators to "prompt for consent on the secure desktop" (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 2).
entries.rationale: The default (5) only prompts for non-Windows binaries; value 2 prompts for every elevation on the isolated secure desktop. Paranoid presets can raise this to 1 (prompt for credentials).

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode

sideEffects: Administrators get a consent dialog for elevations that previously ran silently.

entries.title: Prompt standard users for credentials on the secure desktop
entries.description: Sets the elevation prompt for standard users to "prompt for credentials on the secure desktop" (ConsentPromptBehaviorUser = 1), so a standard user can still elevate by entering an admin password.
entries.rationale: The org-hardening value is 0 (automatically deny), but on a single-user home PC where the account is a standard user that blocks all installs. Value 1 keeps elevation possible while still using the secure desktop. Strict/org presets use 0.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users

sideEffects: The stricter org value (0) would auto-deny all standard-user elevation, blocking installs on single-user standard-account PCs; this entry uses 1 to preserve elevation on the secure desktop.

entries.title: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation
entries.description: Enables installer detection heuristics (EnableInstallerDetection = 1) so setup programs trigger a UAC prompt.
entries.rationale: Ensures legacy installers are elevated through UAC rather than silently failing or writing to virtualized locations. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS enable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation

entries.title: Only elevate UIAccess apps from secure locations
entries.description: Requires UIAccess applications to run from secure locations (EnableSecureUIAPaths = 1) before they can bypass the secure desktop.
entries.rationale: Prevents malware in a user-writable path from claiming UIAccess to interact with elevated windows. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS enable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations

entries.title: Show UAC prompts on the secure desktop
entries.description: Switches to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation (PromptOnSecureDesktop = 1), isolating the prompt from other running software.
entries.rationale: The secure desktop stops other processes from spoofing or auto-clicking the UAC dialog. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS enable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation

sideEffects: Some remote-control tools (certain VNC/RMM agents) cannot see or interact with the UAC prompt unless they run as SYSTEM.

entries.title: Virtualize file and registry write failures
entries.description: Redirects legacy apps' writes to protected file and registry locations into per-user virtualized stores (EnableVirtualization = 1).
entries.rationale: Lets older applications run as a standard user without silently corrupting system-wide state or demanding elevation. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS enable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations

entries.title: Only elevate signed and validated executables
entries.description: Requires that any executable requesting elevation is signed and its signature validates (ValidateAdminCodeSignatures = 1).
entries.rationale: Blocks elevation of unsigned or tampered binaries. This is a Paranoid-tier control because it also blocks legitimate unsigned tools.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated

sideEffects: Breaks elevation of any unsigned installer or tool, including many open-source utilities, portable apps and developer builds.

entries.title: Do not enumerate administrator accounts on elevation
entries.description: Stops the credential UI from listing administrator account names when a standard user elevates (EnumerateAdministrators = 0).
entries.rationale: Not showing admin usernames removes free reconnaissance for an attacker at the elevation prompt. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS set it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Credential User Interface\Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation

entries.title: Hide the password reveal button
entries.description: Removes the eye/reveal button from password fields (DisablePasswordReveal = 1) so entered passwords cannot be shown as plaintext.
entries.rationale: Prevents shoulder-surfing of typed passwords. Microsoft baseline and CIS set it; low UX cost.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Credential User Interface\Do not display the password reveal button

sideEffects: Users can no longer un-mask a password field to check what they typed.

entries.title: Prevent security questions for local accounts
entries.description: Blocks the use of security questions as a recovery method for local accounts (NoLocalPasswordResetQuestions = 1).
entries.rationale: Security questions are weak, guessable recovery factors. Microsoft baseline and CIS set it. Users must rely on other recovery methods.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Credential User Interface\Prevent the use of security questions for local accounts

sideEffects: Users cannot set or use security questions to reset a local password and need another recovery method.

entries.title: Enable UAC Administrator protection (24H2+)
entries.description: Selects the new "Admin Approval Mode with Administrator protection" type (TypeOfAdminApprovalMode = 2), giving each elevation a just-in-time, system-managed shadow admin token gated by Windows Hello.
entries.rationale: Administrator protection removes the always-available admin token from the interactive session, so malware cannot silently reuse it. Rolled out on Windows 11 24H2/25H2; verify the feature is present on the build before applying.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Configure type of Admin Approval Mode

sideEffects: Elevated apps run under a separate system-managed admin profile, so per-user paths and HKCU state differ in the elevated context; some legacy admin tools and installers that assume the same profile break.
Windows Hello is required to authorize each elevation prompt.

entries.title: Lock the machine after 15 minutes idle
entries.description: Sets the machine inactivity limit to 900 seconds (InactivityTimeoutSecs) so Windows locks automatically after 15 minutes with no input.
entries.rationale: Stops an unattended, unlocked session from being used. STIG, Microsoft baseline, CIS and ACSC all cap this at 15 minutes.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit

sideEffects: The screen locks during long reads or presentations; the user cannot set a longer idle limit than the policy allows.

entries.title: Require a password when the PC wakes
entries.description: Requires a password on resume from sleep on both AC and battery power by setting ACSettingIndex and DCSettingIndex to 1 under the wake power-policy GUID.
entries.rationale: Without this, a device woken from sleep goes straight to the desktop. Microsoft baseline, STIG and CIS require a password on wake.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Power Management\Sleep Settings\Require a password when a computer wakes

entries.title: Do not display the last signed-in user
entries.description: Hides the previously signed-in username on the logon screen (DontDisplayLastUserName = 1) so it must be typed each time.
entries.rationale: Removes a free username for an attacker at the console. CIS and ACSC recommend it. This is friction on single-user PCs, so it is a Strict-tier control.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Interactive logon: Do not display last signed-in

sideEffects: Users must type their username at every sign-in; Windows Hello still works after the name is entered, but the convenience flow is interrupted.

entries.title: Require Ctrl+Alt+Del to sign in
entries.description: Requires the secure attention sequence before the logon prompt appears by setting DisableCAD to 0.
entries.rationale: Ctrl+Alt+Del invokes the trusted logon path, defeating credential-harvesting fake logon screens. Microsoft baseline and CIS require it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL

sideEffects: Adds a keystroke before sign-in; on tablets and Windows Hello face-unlock devices this is extra friction.

entries.title: Require sign-in before shutting down
entries.description: Removes the shutdown control from the sign-in screen by setting ShutdownWithoutLogon to 0.
entries.rationale: Stops someone at the lock screen from shutting the machine down (a minor availability and forensics protection). CIS recommends it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on

sideEffects: The power/shutdown button is removed from the lock screen; users must sign in first, which is inconvenient on laptops.

entries.title: Disable automatic sign-in after a restart (ARSO)
entries.description: Turns off Automatic Restart Sign-On (DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn = 1) so Windows does not silently sign the last user back in and relaunch their apps after an update restart.
entries.rationale: ARSO restores the interactive session without re-authenticating, which weakens the value of the lock screen after an update. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS disable it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Logon Options\Sign-in and lock last interactive user automatically after a restart

sideEffects: After a Windows Update restart the machine lands on the lock screen instead of auto-relaunching the previous apps; BitLocker devices lose the auto sign-in convenience.

entries.title: Disable lock-screen camera, slideshow and app notifications
entries.description: Blocks the lock-screen camera (NoLockScreenCamera), the lock-screen slideshow (NoLockScreenSlideshow) and app notifications on the lock screen (DisableLockScreenAppNotifications) so no content or previews are shown before sign-in.
entries.rationale: Notification previews and slideshow images can leak information from a locked device; the lock-screen camera is an unauthenticated entry point. Microsoft baseline (camera/slideshow), STIG and CIS set these.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Control Panel\Personalization\Prevent enabling lock screen camera

sideEffects: No notification previews, slideshow or camera are available on the lock screen.

entries.title: Restrict Windows Ink and voice activation above the lock screen
entries.description: Keeps the Windows Ink Workspace enabled but not available above the lock screen (AllowWindowsInkWorkspace = 1) and blocks apps from being activated by voice while the device is locked (LetAppsActivateWithVoiceAboveLock = 2).
entries.rationale: Ink and voice surfaces above the lock screen can be abused to interact with a locked device. STIG, Microsoft baseline and CIS restrict them.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Ink Workspace\Allow Windows Ink Workspace

sideEffects: Pen users can no longer open the Ink Workspace from the lock screen; voice assistants cannot activate apps while locked.

entries.title: Do not show the network selection UI at logon
entries.description: Removes the network (Wi-Fi) selection UI from the sign-in screen by setting DontDisplayNetworkSelectionUI to 1.
entries.rationale: The lock-screen network UI lets an unauthenticated person reconfigure connectivity. STIG and CIS remove it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Logon\Do not display network selection UI

sideEffects: A laptop joining a new Wi-Fi network cannot pick it from the lock screen; the user must sign in first using cached or local credentials.

entries.title: Block showing account details on the sign-in screen
entries.description: Prevents the sign-in screen from displaying account details such as the email address (BlockUserFromShowingAccountDetailsOnSignin = 1).
entries.rationale: Hides the account's email/identity from anyone at the lock screen. Microsoft baseline and CIS set it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Logon\Block user from showing account details on sign-in

sideEffects: The account email is no longer shown on the sign-in screen.

entries.title: Remove "Run as different user" from context menus
entries.description: Suppresses the "Run as different user" shell verb for batch, command, executable and MMC files by setting SuppressionPolicy to 4096 on each file class.
entries.rationale: Removes an easy path to launch processes under other credentials from Explorer. STIG and the Microsoft Security Guide recommend it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MS Security Guide\Remove 'Run as different user' from context menus

sideEffects: The "Run as different user" entry disappears from the right-click menu for scripts, executables and MMC consoles.
